goal: Understand SQL window functions well enough to rewrite my self-join reports
interpretation: In one lunch break, the learner can read and write window functions (OVER/PARTITION BY, ROW_NUMBER/RANK, running totals with frames, LAG/LEAD) and spot which self-join reports to rewrite with them.
assumptions: Self-join reports are typically previous-row comparisons, top-N per group, and running totals, so those patterns are prioritised.
Videos that don't use PostgreSQL are acceptable here because window-function syntax is the same.
Video summaries are the only evidence of content. The picks were not watched end to end.

sub_topics.title: OVER, PARTITION BY and how windows differ from GROUP BY
sub_topics.why: The core mental model. It makes the move away from self-joins and GROUP BY possible.

sub_topics.title: ROW_NUMBER / RANK / DENSE_RANK and top-N per group
sub_topics.why: Replaces self-joins and correlated subqueries that find the top row in each group.

sub_topics.title: LAG / LEAD for previous/next-row comparisons
sub_topics.why: Directly replaces the classic self-join on id-1 or on the previous month.

sub_topics.title: Running totals and moving averages with window frames
sub_topics.why: Replaces self-joins that use a <= condition to build cumulative totals.

picks.title: SQL Window Functions Explained: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD
picks.reason: It covers every gap in one pass: OVER/PARTITION BY, the ranking functions, LAG/LEAD, running totals and ROWS BETWEEN frames. It also shows report-style patterns (top-N per group, month-over-month growth) and common mistakes, and it uses an online store database.

evidence.quote: A window function keeps every row and adds a calculated value next to each one.
Partition by decides which rows belong together. Order by decides the sequence inside each group.
LAG fetches the value from the row before, LEAD fetches the row after.
ROWS BETWEEN controls exactly which rows count.
Forgetting ORDER BY inside OVER. LAG and running totals need a defined order or the results are random.

picks.confidence_note: The summary matches the learner's needs closely. It is a small channel, so I can't judge teaching quality beyond the transcript.

picks.title: Window Functions in PostegreSQL
picks.reason: It is a second walkthrough in PostgreSQL. It reinforces the comparison with GROUP BY and PARTITION BY, then works through running and rolling sums with frames. Seeing those queries run in the learner's own database helps them transfer the pattern to their reports.

evidence.quote: When I think of a window function, I actually compare it a lot to something like a group by
We take it row by row, but then we apply it to each row. We don't aggregate it all into one row.
Partition by is kind of like a grouping. We're grouping it by the species, and then we're applying this row number.
This is what's called a rolling sum. As we go down, we're just adding the next row into this total

picks.confidence_note: It overlaps the first video on ranking and does not cover LAG/LEAD. The value is a different dataset and PostgreSQL practice.

warnings: Total is about 29.9 minutes of a 30-minute budget, so there is no slack for pausing. If time runs short, watch only the first video and skip the second.

The two picks overlap on partitions, ranking and running totals. I kept the second because it is PostgreSQL-specific and shows rolling sums on a different dataset. It has no LAG/LEAD, so the first video is the only coverage of that topic.

Neither video explicitly walks through rewriting a self-join as a window function. The month-over-month and top-N patterns in the first video are the closest match, so you will need to apply the rewrite to your own reports.
Among the alternatives, techTFQ (24.9 min) covers LAG/LEAD but has no running totals, and it would have pushed the plan over budget alongside a second video.
